reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived from the offset map: Ps 92 is shift+1, so web:Ps.92.0 = oshb:Ps.92.1 (is_counted_title true) and web:Ps.92.1-Ps.92.3 = oshb:Ps.92.2-Ps.92.4; all four boundary_evidence_refs pairings are arithmetically correct. The title quote מִזְמ֥וֹר שִׁ֗יר לְי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.92.1 and the WEB title is verbatim. The exclusivity claim was re-swept independently rather than trusted: a book-wide WEB phrase sweep for the word Sabbath returns 1 verse, Ps.92.0 (sweep: 1 verse), so the only-title claim holds and its object and unit are named. The closing seam is well warranted -- oshb:Ps.92.5 opens with a causal particle plus a 2ms finite verb, the first finite verb after the series. What fails is the description of the series itself, which is the row's stated warrant for one syntactic unit. Span, unit_type and confidence are otherwise sound.

challenges.claim: The row's syntactic warrant miscounts the opening series: it names to play the instruments at web:Ps.92.3 = oshb:Ps.92.4 as the third of 'Three parallel infinitive clauses' when oshb:Ps.92.4 contains no infinitive at all, and it omits the actual third lamed-infinitive of the chain, which stands at oshb:Ps.92.2.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.2 (= web:Ps.92.1) carries TWO lamed-infinitives, לְהֹד֥וֹת and וּלְזַמֵּ֖ר; oshb:Ps.92.3 (= web:Ps.92.2) carries the third, לְהַגִּ֣יד. oshb:Ps.92.4 (= web:Ps.92.3) reads עֲֽלֵי עָ֭שׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי נָ֑בֶל עֲלֵ֖י הִגָּי֣וֹן בְּכִנּֽוֹר -- three prepositional phrases headed by the same preposition plus a noun; the verse holds 7 whitespace-delimited tokens and 0 lamed-prefixed infinitive tokens (token count over the maqaf-free source bytes). The English witness agrees: WEB renders that verse instrumentally, “with the ten-stringed lute, with the harp, and with the melody of the lyre.” (web:Ps.92.3), not as a purpose clause. Every Hebrew span here collates at byte tier against its cited ref. observed_substrate_signals[1] repeats the same error when it runs the infinitive chain through web:Ps.92.3 = oshb:Ps.92.4.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived clean. Arithmetic: all five boundary_evidence_refs pairings are correct for shift+1 (web:Ps.92.4-Ps.92.8 = oshb:Ps.92.5-Ps.92.9). The opening Hebrew quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.92.5 and its gloss covers exactly the three quoted words; the WEB quote at web:Ps.92.5 is verbatim. Both seams verify independently: oshb:Ps.92.5 opens with a causal particle plus a 2ms finite verb after a verse that has no finite verb at all, and oshb:Ps.92.9 opens with the psalm's one independent 2ms pronoun, so the close at web:Ps.92.7 is tier-1 supported from both sides. The rejected_alternative survives its own test: oshb:Ps.92.7 states that the fool does not know and oshb:Ps.92.8 supplies what he does not know, one clause completing the other. No marks claims, no universals flagged, register clean, no quote/gloss desync. One observation, not a defect in anything the row asserts: the epithet כָּל פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן closing this row's last verse (oshb:Ps.92.8 = web:Ps.92.7) recurs skeleton-identically as כָּל at oshb:Ps.92.10 = web:Ps.92.9, just past the seam. A skeleton sweep of that phrase returns 7 verses book-wide (Ps.5.6, Ps.6.9, Ps.14.4, Ps.92.8, Ps.92.10, Ps.94.4, Ps.101.8; MT refs), two of them inside this psalm (sweep: 7 verses). The two tokens differ at accent_stripped tier (U+0591 etnachta at oshb:Ps.92.8 against U+05BD meteg at oshb:Ps.92.10), each collating at byte tier against its own verse and skeleton tier against the other. Because the repetition brackets rather than crosses the driver verse oshb:Ps.92.9, it does not argue against the seam; disclosing it would be a seam-pair edit shared with the row opening at web:Ps.92.8.

Arithmetic verified: web:Ps.92.8 = oshb:Ps.92.9, web:Ps.92.11 = oshb:Ps.92.12 and web:Ps.92.12 = oshb:Ps.92.13 are all correct for shift+1, and both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier. The opening driver is real and I confirmed the supporting claim from the bytes: וְאַתָּ֥ה מָר֗וֹם at oshb:Ps.92.9 is the psalm's one independent second-person pronoun -- a token check over the psalm's 16 MT verses returns that pronoun spelling in 1 verse (oshb:Ps.92.9), while the psalm's bound 2ms suffixes sit in 5 verses (oshb:Ps.92.2, 92.3, 92.5, 92.6, 92.10; count unit: verses). The closing driver at oshb:Ps.92.13 is a genuine fronted third-person subject, and medium confidence is appropriate. Between those two sound seams sit three checkable defects: the address frame the row claims for the whole span does not reach its last verse, the content attributed to a two-verse ref sits in only one of them, one gloss is shorter than its quote, and one out-of-span argued pair is missing from the refs array. Separately noted: the verdancy adjective at oshb:Ps.92.11 = web:Ps.92.10 recurs inside the following span, but the disclosure gap for that link is filed against the row that asserts its absence rather than here.

challenges.claim: The 'one address-governed unit' warrant and the content-to-ref pairing both fail at the row's last verse: web:Ps.92.11 carries no second-person form at all, and neither of the two things the row attributes to web:Ps.92.10-Ps.92.11 (exaltation, anointing) occurs there -- both are confined to web:Ps.92.10.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.12 (= web:Ps.92.11) reads וַתַּבֵּ֥ט עֵינִ֗י בְּשׁ֫וּרָ֥י בַּקָּמִ֖ים עָלַ֥י מְרֵעִ֗ים תִּשְׁמַ֥עְנָה אָזְנָֽי: its referents are first-person (עֵינִ֗י, עָלַ֥י, אָזְנָֽי), and across the verse's 8 tokens there are 0 second-person forms -- no 2ms suffix, no 2ms pronoun, no 2ms verb. WEB agrees, “My eye has also seen my enemies. My ears have heard of the wicked enemies who rise up against me.” (web:Ps.92.11). The exaltation and the anointing are both inside oshb:Ps.92.11 (= web:Ps.92.10) alone: וַתָּ֣רֶם כִּרְאֵ֣ים קַרְנִ֑י בַּ֝לֹּתִ֗י בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן רַעֲנָֽן. The second-person frame the row opens at web:Ps.92.8 therefore stops at web:Ps.92.10, leaving a rival seam at web:Ps.92.10|web:Ps.92.11 that the row neither takes nor answers. All Hebrew here collates at byte tier.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync in observed_substrate_signals[1]: the Hebrew quote runs three words but the gloss covers only two of them.
challenges.evidence: The row quotes צַ֭דִּיק כַּתָּמָ֣ר יִפְרָ֑ח (oshb:Ps.92.13, byte tier) and glosses it 'the righteous shall flourish', dropping כַּתָּמָ֣ר. WEB renders the same three words “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree.” (web:Ps.92.12). challenges.claim: Refs-mirror gap: the rationale argues two verses outside the row's span -- the bare mention 'vv.6-7', which resolves against the span psalm to web:Ps.92.6 and web:Ps.92.7 -- but boundary_evidence_refs carries no entry for either.
challenges.evidence: span = Ps.92.8-Ps.92.11; boundary_evidence_refs = web:Ps.92.8 = oshb:Ps.92.9, web:Ps.92.11 = oshb:Ps.92.12, web:Ps.92.12 = oshb:Ps.92.13. reviews.reasoning: Arithmetic verified: web:Ps.92.1 = oshb:Ps.92.2, web:Ps.92.12 = oshb:Ps.92.13 and web:Ps.92.15 = oshb:Ps.92.16 are all correct. The Hebrew quote collates at byte tier and its gloss covers the full quoted span here. The opening seam is well warranted by the fronted third-person subject and the span closes the psalm, so tiling is not in question. Two checkable defects sit in the supporting prose: the device_notes gets the psalm's frame wrong in a way the bytes settle, and the substrate signal asserts an absence the preceding span contradicts. Disclosure observation, deliberately not filed as a challenge: this span's last verse oshb:Ps.92.16 is the only ketiv/qere verse in Psalm 92 (pmarks_Ps.json kq, 1 note), carrying the unpointed ketiv token inline before the pointed qere. The row quotes only the WEB of that verse and makes no Hebrew claim about it, so the brief's rule as worded (disclosed when quoted) is not triggered; the strategy's wording (when a quoted span crosses one) would trigger it, and that divergence is reported upward rather than charged to the row.

challenges.claim: device_notes asserts the closing inclusio is in theme 'rather than repeated wording', but the psalm's closing purpose infinitive is the same word as the infinitive opening web:Ps.92.2 -- the frame IS repeated wording, and the row has paired the closing verse with the wrong opening verse.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.16 (= web:Ps.92.15) opens לְ֭הַגִּיד כִּֽי יָשָׁ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה; oshb:Ps.92.3 (= web:Ps.92.2) opens לְהַגִּ֣יד בַּבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְֽדֶּ֑ךָ. The two leading tokens לְ֭הַגִּיד and לְהַגִּ֣יד are identical at accent_stripped tier, differing only in accent (U+05A3 munach inside the word at oshb:Ps.92.3 against U+05AD dehi at oshb:Ps.92.16); each collates at byte tier against its own verse. A skeleton sweep of that infinitive spelling returns 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) -- oshb:Ps.92.3 and oshb:Ps.92.16, both inside this psalm and nowhere else in the book. WEB preserves the frame at “to show that Yahweh is upright.” (web:Ps.92.15).

challenges.claim: The substrate signal's 'absent from the preceding span' overstates: a byte-true verdancy link straddles the row's own opening seam, since the adjective this span uses of the righteous already qualifies the oil in the preceding span.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.92.11 (= web:Ps.92.10, inside the preceding span) ends בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן; oshb:Ps.92.15 (= web:Ps.92.14, in-span) ends דְּשֵׁנִ֖ים -- singular and plural of the same adjective. Skeleton sweeps, named per attested spelling because final-letter allography splits them: the final-nun singular spelling returns 3 verses book-wide (Ps.37.35, Ps.52.10, Ps.92.11; MT refs) and the plural spelling returns 1 verse (Ps.92.15) (sweep: 3 verses and 1 verse). Both tokens collate at byte tier. WEB keeps the link visible at “They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green,” (web:Ps.92.14). Under the cross-seam-cohesion rule the link needs disclosure; the row asserts absence instead, and the assertion carries no sweep.

reviews.reasoning: I re-ran every sweep this row leans on rather than trusting it, and the sweeps are correct: a skeleton sweep of the divine-name-plus-malak sequence returns 6 verses book-wide (Ps.10.16, Ps.29.10, Ps.93.1, Ps.96.10, Ps.97.1, Ps.99.1; sweep: 6 verses), all six identity psalms so MT and WEB numbering coincide and the bare refs need no dual-cite; the pointed bytes do split them as the row says, with the noun at oshb:Ps.10.16 and oshb:Ps.29.10 against the verb at oshb:Ps.93.1, oshb:Ps.96.10, oshb:Ps.97.1 and oshb:Ps.99.1 (sweep: 4 verses), and Ps 93 does precede the other three. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier and both WEB quotes are verbatim. The whole_psalm unit_type is policy-compliant for a five-verse psalm and I am not contesting the span. What I contest is the substrate the row files under it: the row's central negative claim about the psalm is false on the bytes and on the row's own WEB quotes, and the rejected_alternative rests on that same false premise, which leaves the rival seam it names standing and makes the high confidence unsupported.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal that 'the psalm's five verses carry no second-person address' is false: 2 of the psalm's 5 verses carry second-person morphology, including an explicit independent pronoun, a third carries a direct vocative, and the row's own quoted WEB text shows it.
challenges.evidence: Ps 93 is an identity psalm, so web and MT numbering coincide throughout. A token check over the 5 verses returns 2ms suffixes or an independent 2ms pronoun in 2 verses (oshb:Ps.93.2, oshb:Ps.93.5; count unit: verses). oshb:Ps.93.2 = נָכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֲךָ֣ מֵאָ֑ז מֵֽעוֹלָ֣ם אָֽתָּה -- a 2ms suffix on כִּסְאֲךָ֣ plus the independent 2ms pronoun אָֽתָּה. oshb:Ps.93.5 opens עֵֽדֹתֶ֨יךָ נֶאֶמְנ֬וּ מְאֹ֗ד לְבֵיתְךָ֥ נַאֲוָה קֹ֑דֶשׁ -- 2ms suffixes on עֵֽדֹתֶ֨יךָ and on לְבֵיתְךָ֥. oshb:Ps.93.3 opens with a vocative, נָשְׂא֤וּ נְהָר֨וֹת יְֽהוָ֗ה. WEB carries the same second person in the very phrases the row quotes: “Your throne is established from long ago.” (web:Ps.93.2) and “Your statutes stand firm.” (web:Ps.93.5). All Hebrew here collates at byte tier. check_universals independently flags this signal and the two claims built on it as unswept negatives.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative is killed by the same false premise and so fails the test it claims to apply: the split it dismisses at web:Ps.93.2 is exactly where the psalm's third-person proclamation turns into second-person address, so the rival seam is left unanswered and the high confidence is uncalibrated.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.93.1 is third-person throughout: יְהוָ֣ה מָלָךְ֮ גֵּא֪וּת לָ֫בֵ֥שׁ לָבֵ֣שׁ יְ֭הוָה עֹ֣ז הִתְאַזָּ֑ר אַף תִּכּ֥וֹן תֵּ֝בֵ֗ל בַּל תִּמּֽוֹט. oshb:Ps.93.2 then switches to second person: נָכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֲךָ֣ מֵאָ֑ז מֵֽעוֹלָ֣ם אָֽתָּה. An explicit independent second-person pronoun is the same class of signal that is treated as a boundary driver two psalms earlier at oshb:Ps.92.9 (וְאַתָּ֥ה מָר֗וֹם), so the row cannot dismiss it here by asserting no addressee change. A replacement warrant must survive the address change at oshb:Ps.93.2, or the confidence must drop. All Hebrew collates at byte tier.

reviews.reasoning: Ps 94 is an identity psalm (no counted title; oshb:Ps.94.1 is the first verse), so the bare web: refs in boundary_evidence_refs need no dual-cite and the arithmetic is trivially correct. The opening Hebrew quote אֵל נְקָמ֥וֹת יְהוָ֑ה collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.94.1 and its gloss covers the quoted span; the doubling claim checks out, the invocation standing twice in that verse. Both WEB quotes are verbatim, including the quoted boast at web:Ps.94.7. The closing seam is strong and I am not contesting it: oshb:Ps.94.8 opens with a plural imperative addressed to the dullards, a fresh addressee, and the quotation frame at oshb:Ps.94.7 does open the psalm's first quoted speech, as the row says -- of this span's 7 verses, 1 carries quoted speech in WEB (web:Ps.94.7; count unit: verses). The defect is in how the middle of the span is described: the row places the end of direct address two verses too early and mis-scopes the victim list across a two-verse ref. Seven-verse count and high confidence are otherwise fine.

challenges.claim: Two content-to-ref defects in the rationale: direct address does not stop at web:Ps.94.3 as the row's 'continuing in direct address through' wording implies, and the widow / foreigner / fatherless list attributed to web:Ps.94.5-Ps.94.6 occurs only at web:Ps.94.6.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.94.5 (= web:Ps.94.5) reads עַמְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה יְדַכְּא֑וּ וְֽנַחֲלָתְךָ֥ יְעַנּֽוּ -- two 2ms suffixes (עַמְּךָ֣, וְֽנַחֲלָתְךָ֥) plus the vocative divine name, so the address to Yahweh runs two verses past web:Ps.94.3. WEB agrees: “They break your people in pieces, Yahweh, and afflict your heritage.” (web:Ps.94.5). The three victims are named only in oshb:Ps.94.6, אַ֭לְמָנָה וְגֵ֣ר יַהֲרֹ֑גוּ וִֽיתוֹמִ֣ים יְרַצֵּֽחוּ, rendered “They kill the widow and the alien, and murder the fatherless.” (web:Ps.94.6). Both Hebrew verses collate at byte tier. The seam at web:Ps.94.7|web:Ps.94.8 is not disturbed by this; the strophe's internal description is.

reviews.reasoning: Identity psalm, so the bare refs are correct. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier: the imperative opening at oshb:Ps.94.8 and the macarism at oshb:Ps.94.12. I verified the macarism signal's span-scoped negative independently and it is true -- a token check returns that macarism spelling in 1 verse across the whole psalm's 23 verses, oshb:Ps.94.12, so 1 verse inside web:Ps.94.8-Ps.94.15 and 0 elsewhere in it (count unit: verses) -- though the row ships the claim without the digit-bearing sweep the count-object rule asks for. The WEB quote at web:Ps.94.12 is verbatim, and the opening seam at web:Ps.94.7|web:Ps.94.8 and closing seam at web:Ps.94.15|web:Ps.94.16 are both tier-1 sound. Medium confidence is right. Two defects: the rejected_alternative's only stated warrant is contradicted by the bytes at the exact verse whose seam it dismisses, and the rhetorical-question scope runs one verse long. Note also the disclosure asymmetry -- an in-span return to direct address is explicitly disclosed at web:Ps.94.20 one seam away, but the same phenomenon at web:Ps.94.12 goes unmentioned here.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's sole warrant -- that the beatitude half stays 'addressed to a general audience rather than to Yahweh or in the first person' -- is false at web:Ps.94.12-Ps.94.13, where the text addresses Yah directly, so the rival seam at web:Ps.94.12 is dismissed on a premise the bytes contradict.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.94.12 reads אַשְׁרֵ֤י הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ: a vocative יָּ֑הּ, a 2ms verb governing it, and a 2ms suffix on וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥. WEB agrees and continues the address into the next verse: “Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of your law,” (web:Ps.94.12) and “that you may give him rest from the days of adversity, until the pit is dug for the wicked.” (web:Ps.94.13). oshb:Ps.94.14 then reverts to third person about Yahweh, כִּ֤י לֹא יִטֹּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ. So the span the row calls uniform in register actually runs general-audience imperative (oshb:Ps.94.8-94.11), direct address to Yah (oshb:Ps.94.12-94.13), then third person (oshb:Ps.94.14-94.15). All Hebrew collates at byte tier. A replacement warrant must survive the addressee switch at web:Ps.94.12 in the same edit.

challenges.claim: 'The rebuke's rhetorical questions (web:Ps.94.9-Ps.94.11)' over-scopes by one verse: web:Ps.94.11 is a declarative statement, not a question.

Both Hebrew verses collate at byte tier. The correct scope is web:Ps.94.9-Ps.94.10.

reviews.reasoning: Identity psalm; the three refs are valid and web:Ps.94.1, argued in device_notes outside the span, is present in the array. Both Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier. The eight-verse count and the closing WEB quote at web:Ps.94.23 are correct, and the doubling described in device_notes is real in the Hebrew as well as the English, oshb:Ps.94.23 repeating the verb immediately before naming the divine title, which the row argues only from the English but which the bytes support. challenges.claim: The row mislocates the return of direct address: it says address 'briefly returns' at web:Ps.94.20 and calls that a renewed address, but 2ms forms are already running at web:Ps.94.18 and web:Ps.94.19.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.94.18 ends חַסְדְּךָ֥, carrying a 2ms suffix, and oshb:Ps.94.19 carries תַּ֝נְחוּמֶ֗יךָ, another 2ms suffix, both before oshb:Ps.94.20. Address therefore runs continuously from web:Ps.94.18 through web:Ps.94.20, which also undercuts the rejected_alternative's framing of vv.16-19 as first-person testimony set against the address at v.20. challenges.claim: The signal that web:Ps.94.16 opens 'a rhetorical question absent from the wisdom-instruction span that precedes it' is false as worded -- that span is built out of rhetorical questions -- and if the intended object is the interrogative pronoun alone, the count-object is never named and never swept.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.94.8 closes מָתַ֥י; oshb:Ps.94.9 reads הֲנֹ֣טַֽע אֹ֭זֶן הֲלֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִֽם יֹ֥צֵֽר עַ֝֗יִן הֲלֹ֣א יַבִּֽיט; oshb:Ps.94.10 opens הֲיֹסֵ֣ר גּ֭וֹיִם הֲלֹ֣א יוֹכִ֑יחַ. WEB renders all of them as questions: “you fools, when will you be wise?” (web:Ps.94.8) and “He who implanted the ear, won’t he hear? He who formed the eye, won’t he see?” (web:Ps.94.9). What is actually absent from web:Ps.94.8-Ps.94.15 is the interrogative מִֽי: a token check over the psalm's 23 verses returns that spelling in 1 verse only, oshb:Ps.94.16, with 2 occurrences there and 0 verses inside oshb:Ps.94.8-94.15 (count unit: verses, then occurrences) -- an object the row never names. All Hebrew collates at byte tier.
